listtile.title_alignment: Vertical position of `leading` and `trailing` next to the text: `"threeLine"`, `"titleHeight"`, `"top"`, `"center"` or `"bottom"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.icon_color: Color of the leading and trailing icons. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.text_color: Color of the title, subtitle, leading and trailing text. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.selected_color: Color of the text and icons while `selected`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.selected_tile_color: Background color while `selected`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.focus_color: Background color while the row has keyboard focus. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.splash_color: Color of the ink ripple when the row is tapped. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.enable_feedback: Plays the platform's tap sound and haptic feedback when the row is tapped. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown while the pointer is over the row. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.title_text_style: Text style of a string title. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.subtitle_text_style: Text style of a string subtitle. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.leading_and_trailing_text_style: Text style of string leading and trailing text. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.on_click: Fired when the user taps the row.
listtile.on_long_press: Fired when the user long-presses the row.

menubar.controls: The menus, usually `submenu_button`s, from left to right. The first positional argument sets them.
menubar.style: The bar's look, for example `{ bgcolor: "#f8fafc", elevation: 0, padding: 4 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; on iOS and macOS the bar is a plain strip with a separator line.
menubar.clip_behavior: How the bar clips its content: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.

menuitembutton.content: The entry's label: a string or a control. The first positional argument sets it.
menuitembutton.leading: A control before the label, such as `icon("save")`.
menuitembutton.trailing: A control after the label, such as a keyboard shortcut hint `text("Ctrl+S")`.
menuitembutton.style: The entry's look per state, as for the text buttons. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
menuitembutton.close_on_click: Closes the menu when the entry is clicked (default `true`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
menuitembutton.focus_on_hover: Moves keyboard focus to the entry while a mouse pointer is over it (default `true`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
menuitembutton.overflow_axis: How a label that does not fit is laid out: `"horizontal"` (default) or `"vertical"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
menuitembutton.semantic_label: Text a screen reader reads instead of the entry's label.
menuitembutton.clip_behavior: How the entry clips its content: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
menuitembutton.autofocus: Gives the entry keyboard focus when it first appears (default `false`).
menuitembutton.disabled: Draws the entry dimmed and ignores taps (default `false`).
menuitembutton.on_focus: Fired when the entry gains keyboard focus, for example while a mouse pointer is over it.
menuitembutton.on_blur: Fired when the entry loses keyboard focus.
menuitembutton.on_click: Fired when the user picks the entry. An entry without an `on_click` handler is drawn disabled.
menuitembutton.on_hover: Fired when a mouse pointer moves onto the entry (`event.data` is `true`) and off it (the client sends `false`, which arrives in Ruby as `nil`).

navigationbar.destinations: The destinations, built with `navigation_bar_destination(icon:, label:)`; two to five work best.
navigationbar.selected_index: Index of the highlighted destination, starting at 0 (default 0).
navigationbar.indicator_color: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, the color of the pill behind the selected icon. On iOS and macOS, the color of the selected destination when `active_color` is not set.
navigationbar.indicator_shape: Shape of the pill behind the selected icon, for example `{ _type: "roundedRectangle", radius: 8 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationbar.label_behavior: Which labels show: `"alwaysShow"` (default), `"onlyShowSelected"` or `"alwaysHide"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; the iOS tab bar always shows them.
navigationbar.label_padding: Space around each label. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationbar.elevation: Shadow depth of the bar. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationbar.shadow_color: Color of the bar's shadow. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationbar.surface_tint_color: Color mixed into the background to show elevation. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationbar.overlay_color: Color of the press and hover highlight on a destination, or a hash of states such as `{ pressed: "#ccfbf1" }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationbar.animation_duration: Length of the indicator's animation, in milliseconds. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationbar.active_color: Color of the selected destination's icon and label on iOS and macOS (default the theme's primary color, or `indicator_color`). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
navigationbar.inactive_color: Color of the other destinations on iOS and macOS (default the system inactive gray). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
navigationbar.icon_size: Size of the icons on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels (default 30). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
navigationbar.border: Accepted for compatibility; no client draws it. The iOS tab bar always has a thin separator line on top.
navigationbar.on_change: Fired when the user picks a destination. `event.data` is its index, starting at 0; the client has already set `selected_index` to it.

navigationbardestination.icon: The destination's icon: an icon name or an `icon(...)` control (required).
navigationbardestination.selected_icon: Icon shown instead of `icon` while the destination is selected, such as a filled variant.
navigationbardestination.label: The destination's label, a string.
navigationbardestination.bgcolor: Accepted for compatibility; no client draws it.
navigationbardestination.disabled: Keeps the user from picking this destination (default `false`); `navigation_bar(disabled: true)` turns off every destination. On Android, web, Windows and Linux the destination is drawn dimmed and ignores taps. On iOS and macOS the tab bar draws it like the others and ignores taps on it.
navigationbardestination.tooltip: Text shown when a mouse pointer rests on the destination or the user long-presses it, on Android, web, Windows and Linux; without it the label is shown. The iOS tab bar on iOS and macOS shows no tooltips.

navigationdrawer.controls: The drawer's entries: `navigation_drawer_destination(icon:, label:)` destinations, plus any other controls such as a heading `text` or a `divider`. The first positional argument sets them.
navigationdrawer.selected_index: Index of the highlighted destination, starting at 0 (Ruby sends 0 when you leave it out). On Android, web, Windows and Linux it counts destinations only; on iOS and macOS it counts every entry of `controls`.
navigationdrawer.indicator_color: Color of the highlight behind the selected destination.
navigationdrawer.tile_padding: Space around each destination (default 12 on the left and right; 12 on every side on iOS and macOS).
navigationdrawer.elevation: Shadow depth of the drawer. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationdrawer.indicator_shape: Shape of the highlight behind the selected destination, for example `{ _type: "stadium" }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationdrawer.shadow_color: Color of the drawer's shadow. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationdrawer.surface_tint_color: Color mixed into the background to show elevation. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationdrawer.on_change: Fired when the user picks a destination. `event.data` is the index the drawer uses for `selected_index`; the client has already set `selected_index` to it.
navigationdrawer.on_dismiss: Fired whenever the drawer closes, by the user or from code. Picking a destination does not close it.

navigationdrawerdestination.icon: The destination's icon: an icon name or an `icon(...)` control.
navigationdrawerdestination.selected_icon: Icon shown instead of `icon` while the destination is selected.
navigationdrawerdestination.label: The destination's label, a string.
navigationdrawerdestination.bgcolor: Background color of the destination. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.

navigationrail.group_alignment: Vertical position of the destinations, from -1.0 (top, the default) to 1.0 (bottom). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.selected_index: Index of the highlighted destination, starting at 0. Leave it out for no selection on Android, web, Windows and Linux; iOS and macOS then highlight the first one.
navigationrail.leading: A control above the destinations, such as a `fab`.
navigationrail.trailing: A control below the destinations. On iOS and macOS it sits at the bottom of the rail.
navigationrail.indicator_color: Color of the highlight behind the selected destination.
navigationrail.extended: Shows each label beside its icon instead of under it (default `false`); `label_type` is then ignored. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; on iOS and macOS labels are always beside the icons.
navigationrail.label_type: Which labels show under the icons: `"all"` (default), `"selected"` or `"none"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.min_width: Width of the rail, in logical pixels (default 80). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.min_extended_width: Width of the rail while `extended`, in logical pixels (default 256). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.elevation: Shadow depth of the rail. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.indicator_shape: Shape of the highlight behind the selected icon. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.use_indicator: Draws the highlight behind the selected icon. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.selected_label_text_style: Text style of the selected destination's label, for example `{ weight: "bold" }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.unselected_label_text_style: Text style of the other labels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationrail.on_change: Fired when the user picks a destination. `event.data` is its index, starting at 0; the client has already set `selected_index` to it.

navigationraildestination.icon: The destination's icon: an icon name or an `icon(...)` control (required).
navigationraildestination.selected_icon: Icon shown instead of `icon` while the destination is selected.
navigationraildestination.label: The destination's label: a string or a control (required).
navigationraildestination.padding: Space around the destination. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationraildestination.indicator_color: Color of the highlight behind this destination's icon when it is selected, instead of the rail's. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
navigationraildestination.indicator_shape: Shape of that highlight. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.

outlinedbutton.content: The label: a string or a control. The first positional argument sets it.
outlinedbutton.icon: Icon shown before the label: an icon name or an `icon(...)` control. On Android, web, Windows and Linux a button with an `icon` also needs `content` (it shows an error box without one); use an [`icon_button`](/docs/control-icon-button) for an icon alone.
outlinedbutton.bgcolor: Background color. On iOS and macOS the outlined button uses it as is. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it only takes effect together with `style:`, so set `style: { bgcolor: ... }` there.
outlinedbutton.color: Color of the label. On iOS and macOS the outlined button uses it as is. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it only takes effect together with `style:`, so set `style: { color: ... }` there.
outlinedbutton.style: The look of the button per state, for example `{ bgcolor: "#0f766e", color: "white", padding: 16, shape: { _type: "roundedRectangle", radius: 8 } }`. Common keys are `color`, `bgcolor`, `icon_color`, `overlay_color`, `elevation`, `padding`, `side`, `shape`, `text_style` and `minimum_size`; a color may be a hash of states such as `{ hovered: "#115e59", default: "#0f766e" }`. On Android, web, Windows and Linux this is the only way to style the button. On iOS and macOS the button reads the same keys, and a key set here wins over the top-level keyword.
outlinedbutton.clip_behavior: How the button clips its content: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. On iOS and macOS it applies only when `style` sets a `shape` or `side`, `elevation` is above 0, or `style` sets `overlay_color`.
outlinedbutton.autofocus: Gives the button keyboard focus when it first appears (default `false`).
outlinedbutton.url: A link the client opens in the browser when the button is clicked, before `on_click` fires.
outlinedbutton.alignment: Where the label sits inside the button on iOS and macOS, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1.0 to 1.0, for example `{ x: -1, y: 0 }` for the left edge (default the center). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { alignment: ... }` there.
outlinedbutton.border_radius: Corner radius of the button on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels, or per corner as `{ top_left:, top_right:, bottom_left:, bottom_right: }` (default 8). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; give `style:` a `shape` there.
outlinedbutton.padding: Space around the label on iOS and macOS; without it the button uses the padding of its `size`. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { padding: ... }` there.
outlinedbutton.min_size: Minimum width and height of the button on iOS and macOS, for example `{ width: 120, height: 44 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { minimum_size: ... }` there.
outlinedbutton.mouse_cursor: Mouse cursor over the button on iOS and macOS (iPad with a pointer, Mac), for example `"click"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { mouse_cursor: ... }` there.
outlinedbutton.focus_color: Color of the focus highlight on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; there the focus color is the `focused` state of `style: { overlay_color: ... }`.
outlinedbutton.disabled_bgcolor: Background color while `disabled` on iOS and macOS (default the system tertiary fill). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use a `disabled` state in `style: { bgcolor: ... }` there.
outlinedbutton.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, the button fades to while pressed on iOS and macOS (default 0.4). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; Material buttons show an ink ripple.
outlinedbutton.size: Size of the button on iOS and macOS: `"small"`, `"medium"` or `"large"` (the default); it sets the default padding and text size. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
outlinedbutton.on_click: Fired when the button is pressed. Not fired while `disabled`.
outlinedbutton.on_long_press: Fired when the button is pressed and held. Not fired while `disabled`.
outlinedbutton.on_hover: Fired when a mouse pointer moves onto the button (`event.data` is `true`) and off it (the client sends `false`, which arrives in Ruby as `nil`). Touch input never fires it.
outlinedbutton.on_focus: Fired when the button gains keyboard focus.
outlinedbutton.on_blur: Fired when the button loses keyboard focus.

outlinediconbutton.icon: The icon: an icon name such as `"add"` or the symbol `:add`, a `Ruflet::MaterialIcons` constant, or an `icon(...)` control. The first positional argument sets it.
outlinediconbutton.icon_size: Size of the icon, in logical pixels (Ruby sends 24 when you leave it out).
outlinediconbutton.selected: Draws the button in its selected state: `selected_icon` and `selected_icon_color` replace `icon` and `icon_color`, and on Android, web, Windows and Linux the outlined button changes its fill. The client does not toggle it; update it from `on_click`.
outlinediconbutton.bgcolor: Background color of the button on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; set `style: { bgcolor: ... }` there.
outlinediconbutton.style: The look per state on Android, web, Windows and Linux, as for the text buttons: for example `{ bgcolor: "#e0f2fe", icon_color: "#0369a1" }`. On iOS and macOS the button reads `bgcolor`, `color`, `icon_color`, `icon_size`, `padding`, `side`, `shape`, `alignment`, `elevation`, `minimum_size`, `fixed_size`, `maximum_size`, `mouse_cursor`, `enable_feedback` and `overlay_color` from it.
outlinediconbutton.highlight_color: Color of the button while it is pressed. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; iOS and macOS buttons fade instead.
outlinediconbutton.hover_color: Color of the button while a mouse pointer is over it. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
outlinediconbutton.splash_color: Color of the ink ripple when the button is pressed. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
outlinediconbutton.splash_radius: Radius of the ink ripple, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
outlinediconbutton.size_constraints: Minimum and maximum size of the button, for example `{ min_width: 48, min_height: 48 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; on iOS and macOS use `style: { minimum_size: ... }`.
outlinediconbutton.visual_density: Compactness of the button: `"compact"`, `"comfortable"`, `"standard"` or `"adaptivePlatformDensity"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
outlinediconbutton.selected_icon: Icon shown instead of `icon` while `selected` is true.
outlinediconbutton.selected_icon_color: Color of the icon while `selected` is true.
outlinediconbutton.enable_feedback: Plays the platform's click sound or haptic tap when the button is pressed.
outlinediconbutton.alignment: Where the icon sits inside the button, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1.0 to 1.0. Ruby sends `"center"` when you leave it out, which the 0.0.23 client cannot read (see the page); pass `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`.
outlinediconbutton.padding: Space around the icon, in logical pixels. Ruby sends `{ "all" => 8 }` when you leave it out, which the 0.0.23 client reads as no padding; pass `padding: 8`.
outlinediconbutton.mouse_cursor: Mouse cursor over the button, for example `"click"`.
outlinediconbutton.focus_color: Color of the button while it has keyboard focus.
outlinediconbutton.autofocus: Gives the button keyboard focus when it first appears (default `false`).
outlinediconbutton.url: A link the client opens in the browser when the button is clicked, before `on_click` fires.
outlinediconbutton.on_click: Fired when the button is pressed. Not fired while `disabled`.
outlinediconbutton.on_long_press: Fired when the button is pressed and held. Not fired while `disabled`.
outlinediconbutton.on_hover: Fired when a mouse pointer moves onto the button (`event.data` is `true`) and off it (the client sends `false`, which arrives in Ruby as `nil`). Touch input never fires it.
outlinediconbutton.on_focus: Fired when the button gains keyboard focus.
outlinediconbutton.on_blur: Fired when the button loses keyboard focus.

popupmenubutton.on_select: Fired when the user picks an item, after the item's own `on_click`. `event.data` is the item's internal control id, so act in each item's `on_click` instead.
popupmenubutton.items: The menu entries, built with `popup_menu_item`. The first positional argument sets them.
popupmenubutton.icon: The button's icon (default a "more" icon: three vertical dots on Android, web, Windows and Linux, an ellipsis on iOS and macOS).
popupmenubutton.content: A control shown as the button instead of the icon, such as `text("Sort")`.
popupmenubutton.padding: Space around the button's icon or content, in logical pixels (default 8).
popupmenubutton.icon_color: Color of the button's icon. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.icon_size: Size of the button's icon, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.bgcolor: Background color of the menu. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.elevation: Shadow depth of the menu. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.shadow_color: Color of the menu's shadow. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.shape: Shape of the menu, for example `{ _type: "roundedRectangle", radius: 12 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.clip_behavior: How the menu clips its entries: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.menu_position: Where the menu opens: `"over"` the button (default) or `"under"` it. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; iOS and macOS open a sheet from the bottom of the screen.
popupmenubutton.menu_padding: Space around the entries inside the menu, for example `{ top: 8, bottom: 8 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.size_constraints: Minimum and maximum size of the menu, for example `{ min_width: 200 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.splash_radius: Radius of the button's ink ripple, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.enable_feedback: Plays the platform's click sound or haptic tap when the button is pressed. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.style: The button's look per state, as for the text buttons, for example `{ bgcolor: "#f1f5f9" }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.popup_animation_style: How the menu animates in and out, for example `{ duration: 200, reverse_duration: 100 }` (milliseconds). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenubutton.on_cancel: Fired when the menu closes without a choice.

popupmenuitem.content: The entry's text: a string or a control. The first positional argument sets it. On iOS and macOS an entry needs it.
popupmenuitem.icon: Icon shown before the text. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenuitem.checked: Shows a check mark beside the entry: `true` or `false` (leave it out for an entry without one). Android, web, Windows and Linux only. The client does not toggle it; update it from `on_click`.
popupmenuitem.padding: Space around the entry's content. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenuitem.label_text_style: Text style of the entry, for example `{ weight: "bold" }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenuitem.mouse_cursor: Mouse cursor over the entry, for example `"click"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
popupmenuitem.on_click: Fired when the user picks the entry. For a `checked` entry, `event.data` is `true` when the entry was unchecked and is now checked; when it was checked the client sends `false`, which arrives in Ruby as `nil`. Other entries send no data.

progressbar.value: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0; leave it unset for an indeterminate bar.
progressbar.bgcolor: Color of the track behind the filled part. On iOS and macOS the default is the system's light gray.
progressbar.color: Color of the filled part. On iOS and macOS the default is the system blue.
progressbar.track_gap: Gap between the filled part and the track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressbar.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design (the default); set `false` for the newer look with a track gap and an end dot. iOS and macOS ignore it.

progressring.animating: On iOS and macOS, spins the indeterminate indicator while true; set `false` to pause it. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.radius: Radius of the activity indicator on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.stroke_cap: Shape of the ring's line ends: `"butt"`, `"round"` or `"square"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the ring's track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.
progressring.value: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0; leave it unset for a spinning indicator.
progressring.progress: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0, the iOS name for `value`; when both are set, `progress` wins.
progressring.bgcolor: Color of the ring's track. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.stroke_width: Thickness of the ring, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.stroke_align: Where the stroke sits on the ring's path: `-1.0` inside, `0.0` centered, `1.0` outside (default: centered, or inside with `year_2023: false`). iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.size_constraints: Size limits of the ring, for example `{ min_width: 48, min_height: 48 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it; size the iOS indicator with `radius`.
progressring.padding: Space around the ring. iOS and macOS ignore it.

reorderablelistview.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels.

responsiverow.columns: Number of virtual columns the row is divided into (default 12); `col` spans count in these.

searchbar.shrink_wrap: Sizes the search view to its suggestions.

semantics.header: Marks the content as a heading for screen readers.
semantics.expanded: Tells screen readers whether the content is expanded.
semantics.on_tap_hint_text: What screen readers say the tap action does, for example "Open".
semantics.on_long_press_hint_text: What screen readers say the long-press action does.
semantics.hint_text: What screen readers say acting on the control does, for example "Opens the message".
semantics.focus: Tells screen readers whether the control has input focus.
semantics.textfield: Tells screen readers that the content is a text field.
semantics.identifier: An identifier for UI tests and platform accessibility tools; screen readers do not announce it.

snackbar.action: The action button: a string label, whose button fires the snack bar's `on_action`, or a `snack_bar_action`, whose own `on_click` fires.
snackbar.duration: How long the snack bar stays visible, in milliseconds (default 4000).
snackbar.content: The message, usually a `text`; required (the first positional argument).
snackbar.persist: Keeps the snack bar open after `duration` until the user taps its action or close icon. On Android, web, Windows and Linux a snack bar with an `action` persists unless you pass `false`; on iOS and macOS it closes after `duration` unless you pass `true`.
snackbar.show_close_icon: Shows a close (x) button that dismisses the snack bar.
snackbar.bgcolor: Background color. On iOS and macOS the default is the system gray.
snackbar.padding: Padding inside the snack bar. On iOS and macOS the default is 16 on the left, 8 on the right and 10 above and below.
snackbar.margin: Space around a `"floating"` snack bar; ignored when `width` is set. On iOS and macOS it is the space around the bar (default 12 at the sides and bottom).
snackbar.width: Width of a `"floating"` snack bar. On iOS and macOS it sets the bar's width.
snackbar.behavior: `"fixed"` (default) spans the bottom edge of the screen; `"floating"` floats above it, and only then are `margin` and `width` used. iOS and macOS ignore it: their snack bar always floats near the bottom.
snackbar.action_overflow_threshold: Fraction of the snack bar's width, from 0.0 to 1.0, that the action may take before it moves below the message (default 0.25). iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.dismiss_direction: Which swipes dismiss the snack bar, for example `"down"` (the default) or `"horizontal"`. iOS and macOS ignore it: the bar cannot be swiped away there.
snackbar.close_icon_color: Color of the close button. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.clip_behavior: How the snack bar clips its content (default `"hardEdge"`). iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.elevation: Shadow depth of the snack bar. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.shape: Shape of the snack bar. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.on_visible: Fired when the snack bar appears.
snackbar.on_dismiss: Fired when the snack bar closes on its own: its time ran out, or the user swiped it away or tapped its action or close icon. Its `open` is `false` again.

snackbaraction.label: Text of the button; required (the first positional argument).
snackbaraction.text_color: Color of the label. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.bgcolor: Background color of the button. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled_text_color: Color of the label once the button has been pressed: an action works only once. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled_bgcolor: Background color once the button has been pressed. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled: Disables the button on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
snackbaraction.on_click: Fired when the user taps the button. On Android, web, Windows and Linux the snack bar then closes; on iOS and macOS it stays until its time runs out.

spinkit.variant: The indicator style; set it with the variant keyword you pass to `spinkit`, such as `three_bounce:`.
spinkit.size: Size of the indicator, in logical pixels (default 50).
spinkit.duration: Length of one animation cycle, in milliseconds.
spinkit.line_width: Line thickness of the `ring` and `dual_ring` variants (default 7) and of `spinning_lines` (default 2), in logical pixels.
spinkit.border_width: Border thickness of the `ripple` variant, in logical pixels (default 6).

stepper.controls: The steps, when a block builds them instead of `steps`.
stepper.steps: The steps, built with `stepper_step(title:, content:)`. The first positional argument sets them; the controls of a block work too.
stepper.current_step: Index of the open step, starting at 0 (Ruby sends 0 when you leave it out). The stepper never changes it by itself: set it from your handlers.
stepper.type: `"vertical"` (Ruby sends it when you leave it out): steps stacked with the open one's content below its title. `"horizontal"`: step titles in a row with the open step's content below.
stepper.show_controls: Shows the Continue and Cancel buttons under the open step (default `true`).
stepper.continue_text: Label of the Continue button (default the platform's "Continue" text).
stepper.cancel_text: Label of the Cancel button (default the platform's "Cancel" text).
stepper.connector_color: Color of the line between steps, or a hash of states such as `{ selected: "#0f766e", default: "#cbd5e1" }`.
stepper.connector_thickness: Thickness of the line between steps, in logical pixels (default 1).
stepper.elevation: Shadow depth of the step header in a horizontal stepper. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
stepper.clip_behavior: How the stepper clips its content: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`.
stepper.on_step_continue: Fired when the user presses Continue. `event.data` is `current_step`. Without a handler the button is disabled.
stepper.on_step_cancel: Fired when the user presses Cancel. `event.data` is `current_step`. Without a handler the button is disabled.
stepper.on_step_tap: Fired when the user taps a step's title. `event.data` is that step's index. Without a handler the titles cannot be tapped.

stepper_step.title: The step's name: a string or a control (required).
stepper_step.subtitle: Smaller text under the title: a string or a control.
stepper_step.label: Short text under the step's circle in a horizontal stepper: a string or a control.
stepper_step.content: The control shown while the step is open, such as a `column` of fields.
stepper_step.state: The step's icon: `"indexed"` (its number, the default), `"editing"` (a pencil), `"complete"` (a check mark), `"disabled"` (greyed out, cannot be tapped) or `"error"` (a warning sign).
stepper_step.is_active: Draws the step's circle in the active color (default `false`). Mark the steps the user has reached.

submenubutton.controls: The entries of the menu this button opens: `menu_item_button`s, more `submenu_button`s for nested menus, or `divider`s. The first positional argument sets them.
submenubutton.content: The button's label: a string or a control.
submenubutton.leading: A control before the label, such as `icon("folder")`.
submenubutton.trailing: A control after the label. On iOS and macOS a chevron is shown when it is not set.
submenubutton.style: The button's look per state, as for the text buttons. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
submenubutton.menu_style: The look of the menu that opens, for example `{ bgcolor: "white", elevation: 4, padding: 8 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
submenubutton.alignment_offset: Moves the menu away from where it would open, as `{ x:, y: }` in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
submenubutton.clip_behavior: How the button clips its content: `"hardEdge"` (default), `"none"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
submenubutton.on_open: Fired when the menu opens. On iOS and macOS the menu opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen.
submenubutton.on_focus: Fired when the button gains keyboard focus.
submenubutton.on_blur: Fired when the button loses keyboard focus.
submenubutton.on_close: Fired when the menu closes, whether or not the user picked an entry. On iOS and macOS picking an entry closes the sheet, which fires it.
submenubutton.on_hover: Fired when a mouse pointer moves onto the button (`event.data` is `true`) and off it (the client sends `false`, which arrives in Ruby as `nil`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.

tab.label: The tab's text: a string or a control. The first positional argument sets it.
tab.icon: An icon shown with the label: above it on Android, web, Windows and Linux, before it on iOS and macOS.
tab.icon_margin: Space between the icon and the label, for example `{ bottom: 4 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.

tabbar.tabs: The tabs, built with `tab(...)`. The first positional argument sets them.
tabbar.indicator_color: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, the color of the line under the selected tab. On iOS and macOS, the color of the sliding thumb behind it.
tabbar.scrollable: Lets the tabs scroll sideways instead of sharing the bar's width (default `true`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only; on iOS and macOS the tabs always share the width.
tabbar.tab_alignment: How the tabs are placed: `"start"`, `"startOffset"`, `"fill"` or `"center"` (default `"start"` when `scrollable`, else `"fill"`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.secondary: Draws a secondary tab bar, for tabs inside a section of the page (default `false`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.indicator: The line under the selected tab, as `{ border_side: { width: 3, color: "#0f766e" }, border_radius: 2, insets: { left: 8, right: 8 } }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.indicator_animation: How the indicator moves between tabs: `"linear"` or `"elastic"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.indicator_size: How wide the indicator is: `"tab"` (the whole tab) or `"label"` (the label only). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.indicator_thickness: Thickness of the indicator line, in logical pixels (default 2). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.divider_color: Color of the line under the whole bar. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.divider_height: Thickness of the line under the whole bar, in logical pixels; 0 hides it. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.label_color: Color of the selected tab's label and icon. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.unselected_label_color: Color of the other tabs' labels and icons. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.label_text_style: Text style of the selected tab's label. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.unselected_label_text_style: Text style of the other labels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.label_padding: Space around each tab's label. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.padding: Space around the whole row of tabs. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.overlay_color: Color of the press and hover highlight on a tab, or a hash of states. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.splash_border_radius: Corner radius of the press highlight. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.enable_feedback: Plays the platform's click sound or haptic tap when a tab is pressed. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.mouse_cursor: Mouse cursor over the tabs, for example `"click"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbar.on_click: Fired when the user picks a tab. `event.data` is its index. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it fires for every tap, even on the selected tab; on iOS and macOS only when the selection moves to another tab.
tabbar.on_hover: Fired when a mouse pointer moves onto or off a tab. `event.data` is a hash with symbol keys: `:hovering` (`true` or `false`) and `:index`.

tabbarview.controls: The pages, one for each tab, in the same order. The first positional argument sets them.
tabbarview.clip_behavior: How the pages are clipped while they slide: `"hardEdge"` (Ruby sends it when you leave it out), `"none"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabbarview.viewport_fraction: Share of the width each page fills (Ruby sends 1.0 when you leave it out); below 1.0 the neighbouring pages show at the edges. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; on iOS and macOS the view shows the selected page and does not swipe.

table.rows: The `table_row` rows; the first positional argument, `rows:` or a block sets them.
table.border_color: Color of the table's lines; nothing is drawn without it.
table.border_width: Width of the lines, in logical pixels (default 1).
table.border_radius: Corner radius of the outer border.

tablerow.controls: The row's cells; the first positional argument, `controls:` or a block sets them. A hidden cell keeps its column.

tabs.content: The layout that holds the `tab_bar` and the `tab_bar_view`, usually a `column`. The first positional argument sets it.
tabs.length: Number of tabs (required). It must equal the number of `tab`s in the `tab_bar` and of pages in the `tab_bar_view`.
tabs.selected_index: Index of the selected tab, starting at 0 (default 0). On Android, web, Windows and Linux a negative index counts from the end. Changing it moves to that tab.
tabs.animation_duration: Length of the move between tabs, in milliseconds (default 100). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
tabs.on_change: Fired when the selected tab changes, from a tap, a swipe or `move_to`. `event.data` is the new index.

textbutton.content: The label: a string or a control. The first positional argument sets it.
textbutton.icon: Icon shown before the label: an icon name or an `icon(...)` control. On Android, web, Windows and Linux a button with an `icon` also needs `content` (it shows an error box without one); use an [`icon_button`](/docs/control-icon-button) for an icon alone.
textbutton.bgcolor: Background color. On iOS and macOS the button uses it as is. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it only takes effect together with `style:`, so set `style: { bgcolor: ... }` there.
textbutton.color: Color of the label. On iOS and macOS the button uses it as is. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it only takes effect together with `style:`, so set `style: { color: ... }` there.
textbutton.style: The look of the button per state, for example `{ bgcolor: "#0f766e", color: "white", padding: 16, shape: { _type: "roundedRectangle", radius: 8 } }`. Common keys are `color`, `bgcolor`, `icon_color`, `overlay_color`, `elevation`, `padding`, `side`, `shape`, `text_style` and `minimum_size`; a color may be a hash of states such as `{ hovered: "#115e59", default: "#0f766e" }`. On Android, web, Windows and Linux this is the only way to style the button. On iOS and macOS the button reads the same keys, and a key set here wins over the top-level keyword.
textbutton.clip_behavior: How the button clips its content: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. On iOS and macOS it applies only when `style` sets a `shape` or `side`, `elevation` is above 0, or `style` sets `overlay_color`.
textbutton.autofocus: Gives the button keyboard focus when it first appears (default `false`).
textbutton.url: A link the client opens in the browser when the button is clicked, before `on_click` fires.
textbutton.alignment: Where the label sits inside the button on iOS and macOS, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1.0 to 1.0, for example `{ x: -1, y: 0 }` for the left edge (default the center). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { alignment: ... }` there.
textbutton.border_radius: Corner radius of the button on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels, or per corner as `{ top_left:, top_right:, bottom_left:, bottom_right: }` (default 8). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; give `style:` a `shape` there.
textbutton.padding: Space around the label on iOS and macOS; without it the button uses the padding of its `size`. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { padding: ... }` there.
textbutton.min_size: Minimum width and height of the button on iOS and macOS, for example `{ width: 120, height: 44 }`. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { minimum_size: ... }` there.
textbutton.mouse_cursor: Mouse cursor over the button on iOS and macOS (iPad with a pointer, Mac), for example `"click"`. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use `style: { mouse_cursor: ... }` there.
textbutton.focus_color: Color of the focus highlight on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; there the focus color is the `focused` state of `style: { overlay_color: ... }`.
textbutton.disabled_bgcolor: Background color while `disabled` on iOS and macOS (default the system tertiary fill). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; use a `disabled` state in `style: { bgcolor: ... }` there.
textbutton.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, the button fades to while pressed on iOS and macOS (default 0.4). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it; Material buttons show an ink ripple.
textbutton.size: Size of the button on iOS and macOS: `"small"`, `"medium"` or `"large"` (the default); it sets the default padding and text size. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
textbutton.on_click: Fired when the button is pressed. Not fired while `disabled`.
textbutton.on_long_press: Fired when the button is pressed and held. Not fired while `disabled`.
textbutton.on_hover: Fired when a mouse pointer moves onto the button (`event.data` is `true`) and off it (the client sends `false`, which arrives in Ruby as `nil`). Touch input never fires it.
textbutton.on_focus: Fired when the button gains keyboard focus.
textbutton.on_blur: Fired when the button loses keyboard focus.

view.route: The view's route, such as `"/settings"`. When `page.views` holds several views, the client shows them as a stack with a back button, and the back gesture fires `page.on_view_pop`.
view.controls: The controls in the view's body, top to bottom. The first positional argument sets them.
view.appbar: The view's top bar, an `app_bar(...)`. `page.appbar` sets it on the page's own view; with `page.views`, give each view its own.
view.bottom_appbar: A `bottom_app_bar(...)` along the bottom of the view. A `navigation_bar` takes its place when both are set.
view.navigation_bar: A `navigation_bar(...)` along the bottom of the view.
view.floating_action_button: A floating action button, usually `fab(...)`, over the view's content.
view.floating_action_button_location: Where the floating action button sits: `"endFloat"` (default), `"centerFloat"`, `"startFloat"`, `"endDocked"`, `"centerDocked"`, `"endTop"` and the other Flutter names, or an offset `{ x:, y: }`. On iOS and macOS a docked location floats above the navigation bar.
view.drawer: A `navigation_drawer(...)` that slides in from the start edge. To open it from code, call `page.invoke` with this view and `"show_drawer"`; `"close_drawer"` closes it.
view.end_drawer: A `navigation_drawer(...)` that slides in from the end edge. To open it from code, call `page.invoke` with this view and `"show_end_drawer"`; `"close_end_drawer"` closes it.
view.bottom_sheet: A control pinned to the bottom of the view, above the navigation bar, such as a `container` with a player or a summary. It stays visible; for a sheet the user dismisses, use `page.show_bottom_sheet`.
view.spacing: Space between the controls of the body, in logical pixels (default 10).
view.vertical_alignment: How the body's controls are placed vertically: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
view.horizontal_alignment: How the body's controls are placed horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"` or `"stretch"`.
view.decoration: A box decoration drawn behind the whole view, app bar included: `{ bgcolor:, gradient:, image:, border:, border_radius:, shadows:, shape: }`.
view.foreground_decoration: A box decoration drawn over the whole view, in the same form as `decoration`.
view.can_pop: Whether the back button and the back gesture may close the view (default `true`). Set it to `false` and handle `on_confirm_pop` to ask first.
view.fullscreen_dialog: Opens the view as a full-screen dialog: it slides up from the bottom, and its app bar shows a close button instead of a back arrow (default `false`).
view.services: Accepted for compatibility; the client does not read it. Add services with `page.services` or `page.service(...)`.
view.refresh_bgcolor: Background color of the pull-to-refresh spinner. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
view.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh spinner settles at while refreshing (default 40). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
view.on_confirm_pop: Fired when the user tries to leave a view that has `can_pop: false`. Answer with `page.invoke(event.control, "confirm_pop", args: { "should_pop" => true })` to close it, or `false` to stay; without an answer the view stays.
view.on_scroll: Fired while the body scrolls (set `scroll:` to make it scrollable), at most every `scroll_interval` milliseconds. `event.data` is a hash with symbol keys: `:event_type` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `:pixels` (the offset), `:min_scroll_extent`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`, plus `:scroll_delta` on updates and `:direction` on user scrolls.
view.on_end_reached: Fired when the user scrolls within `end_reached_threshold` of the end of the body, for loading more. `event.data` is a hash with symbol keys `:pixels`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`.

contextmenu.open: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, shows the entries of `items` (or `actions`) at the middle of `content`; the client does not read `position:` yet. On iOS and macOS the menu cannot be opened from code; it opens only from the user's long press.

tabs.move_to: Selects the tab at `index` (a negative index counts from the end) and fires `on_change`. `duration` (milliseconds) and `curve` shape the animation on Android, web, Windows and Linux.
